title: Trace ids for a collector: one request, one W3C trace, spans for its jobs, model requests and agent steps
request: Phase 1's last observability gap: a request had an id, but a collector (OpenTelemetry, a log store) joins by trace and span ids; the log lines, the events, the jobs a request queued and its model requests shared no id that a tool could follow end to end. Adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.tracing (parse and format the W3C traceparent, derive a trace id from a request id); Ids gains trace, span, parent_span (event v8); the edge continues or derives a trace and answers with a traceparent; events and log lines carry the ids; a job runs in the request's trace in its own span; a model request, an agent step and a tool call are spans; the record is read by trace (an indexed column on PostgreSQL).
plan: The header and the derivation as pure functions in the core.
A trace context in observe that every event and log line reads; a span context manager.
The edge binds the trace and the request's span and answers with a traceparent; the job takes the trace and the request's span as its parent.
Model requests, agent steps and tool calls are spans.
Read by trace on both logs, the finder, the route and the command line; the adapter's stamp for rows that have a request id.

decisions.decision: A request that offers only a trace is known by its first 16 characters.
decisions.why: Logs, the Admin lookup and X-Request-ID already speak in request ids: the trace names it when nothing else does.

decisions.decision: A request id that came without a trace gets a trace derived from it (its SHA-256), so one request id is always one trace.
decisions.why: A collector joins by trace; the main product's rows carry only a request id and must land in the same trace its edge would have made.

decisions.decision: The trace id is a column of its own on PostgreSQL, not a path into the document.
decisions.why: Reading one request's events by trace is the point of the id; the index follows the other id columns.

decisions.decision: An agent step and a tool call get a span when they are recorded, not while they run.
decisions.why: The agent writes its trace row after the step; the span id is what a collector joins by.

change: dclab_core tracing.py (new), experience.py (Ids, v8), adapters/main_product_experience.py (with_trace), CHANGELOG 0.48.0; dclab_rnd observe.py (TRACE, span, log fields), agentic/server.py (the edge), experience/__init__.py (ids from the trace, the origin, the trace filter), experience/finder.py, experience/__main__.py, agentic/pages/sessions.py, jobs/worker.py (the job's span), models/gateway.py (a model request is a span), experience/hooks.py (steps and tool calls), storage/models.py + migration 0019; tests test_tracing.py (new); CORE_INTEGRATION.md, the plan.

findings.defect: The tests shared a client and one trace id: an event from the model-request test was found under the request test's trace.
findings.scenario: The span assertion failed with a span from another test.
findings.fix: A trace of its own per test, and a request that records events (a draft).

findings.defect: Creating a project records no event, so a test that expected the request's events found none.
findings.scenario: assertTrue(events) passed only because another test had left one.
findings.cause: Assumed an event per write route.
findings.fix: The test uses POST /api/drafts, which records draft.created.

findings.defect: An export kept the trace, span and parent span ids, which undo the stripping of the request id.
findings.scenario: The request id is 32 hex characters, so the trace equals it; or a caller sends only a traceparent, so the request id is the trace's first 16 characters; the parent span is the caller's own. export_events removed only user and request.
findings.cause: The list of ids that stay home was written before the trace ids existed.
findings.fix: One list, HOME_IDS: user, request, trace, span, parent span. Exports hold the project and nothing that joins an event to a request or a log line.

findings.defect: A streamed model request and an embedding were not spans of their own: two streams of one turn shared the turn's span.
findings.scenario: Only complete() wrapped the call in a span; stream() (used whenever the Home agent or the intern shows text as it arrives) and embed() sent their model.request events with the outer span and no parent.
findings.cause: The span was put in the one method the first test called.
findings.fix: stream() and embed() take a span around the call; a transport without streaming still goes through complete().

findings.defect: Outside a request or a job every span started its own trace, so a run's steps and model requests never shared one.
findings.scenario: A script, the campaign loop or an evaluation called hooks.from_trace twice with no trace running: each step got a new trace.
findings.cause: span() starts a trace when none runs, and nothing above the steps started one.
findings.fix: A run (agents.runtime.run) and a session (harness.session) are spans, their end event inside; the campaign command line sets one trace for the command.
findings.test: test_tracing RunOutsideARequestTest (a session, a model loop, a session inside a request)

findings.defect: The done-when item that log lines, events and model requests share a trace was tested only at the formatter and by hand.
findings.scenario: Deleting the gateway's span, or the middleware's trace, left every test passing.
findings.cause: The tests called the pieces, not the path.
findings.fix: A request's JSON log line is read and compared with its events' trace and span; the gateway test goes through Gateway.complete, stream and embed.

findings.defect: with_trace said the derived trace is what the edge would have put in the traceparent; that holds only for a request that came without one.
findings.scenario: A request offered a traceparent: the edge names it trace[:16], and a hash of that prefix is not the trace.
findings.cause: The docstring described one of two paths.
findings.fix: The docstring says which path it covers and that the host which kept the header gives the trace itself.

outcome: One request's log lines, events and model requests share a trace id, through the job it queued.
lessons: Give each test its own id when the store is shared; a constant makes tests read each other's events.
A list of ids that stay home is a contract: every id a package adds is added to it or decided about, in the same commit.
risks: Work in a thread the request did not start carries no trace (a context variable does not cross a bare thread).
The model-request usage table keeps no trace id; its event does.
